description: P1 HIGH PRIORITY: Complete Citizen evidence and notification features. Citizens can upload evidence images but cannot VIEW them (no retrieval endpoint). Citizens do not see status change notifications (alerts generated on backend but no UI polling/display). These are partially-implemented features blocking full citizen experience.
steps: 1. EVIDENCE RETRIEVAL BACKEND: Read backend/app/routers/citizen.py and backend/app/routers/operations.py lines ~380 (existing staff image retrieval endpoint as pattern). Add new endpoint GET /api/citizen/reports/{report_id}/evidence/{image_id} with require_csrf dependency.
2. Implement authorization check: Query resq_incidents table to verify reporter_id matches current user (citizen_user dependency). Return 404 if report not owned by citizen.
3. Fetch image metadata: Query resq_incident_images table for storage_key, content_type, original_filename where id=:image_id and incident_id=:report_id.

4. Read file from IMAGE_ROOT (from config.py) using storage_key path. Return FileResponse with appropriate Content-Type, Cache-Control headers (public, max-age=31536000, immutable), and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

5. EVIDENCE RETRIEVAL FRONTEND: Read frontend/src/redesign/pages/CitizenApp.tsx CitizenReportDetailPage component (around line 150-200). Update evidence display section to render tags instead of text-only filenames.
6. Use authenticated fetch pattern: . Add error handling for 404/403.
7. Display evidence metadata alongside images: filename, size, assessment_status badge (COMPLETED, UNAVAILABLE, EXPERIMENTAL).

8. NOTIFICATION DISPLAY FRONTEND: Add alert polling hook to CitizenApp component root (after session check). Poll GET /api/alerts every 30 seconds (endpoint already exists, returns alerts for current user).
9. Track unread count: Filter alerts where read=false, display count in header badge.
10. Add notification badge to CitizenShell header navigation: Notifications {unreadCount > 0 && {unreadCount}}.

11. Create CitizenNotificationsPage route (in CitizenApp router around line 180, after removing old route trap). Display alert list with message, created_at, kind. Add 'Mark read' button that calls PATCH /api/alerts/{alert_id}/read (endpoint exists).
12. Update alert list on mark-read: Decrement unread count, update alert read status in state.
acceptance_criteria: Citizens can view uploaded evidence images on report detail page (not just filenames)
Evidence images load with proper authentication (bearer token in request headers)
Assessment status badge displayed alongside each image (COMPLETED, UNAVAILABLE, etc.)
Only report owner can view evidence (403 for other users, 404 for non-existent reports)
Citizen notification badge appears in header with unread count when alerts exist
Clicking notification badge navigates to /citizen/notifications page with alert list
Alert messages displayed with timestamp and kind (incident_status_changed, verification_submitted, etc.)
Mark read button works: alert marked read, count decrements, alert styling changes
Alert polling works: New alerts appear without page refresh (30s polling interval)
Only citizen's own alerts visible (not all system alerts)
verification: EVIDENCE RETRIEVAL: As authenticated citizen, navigate to /citizen/reports/{id} where report has uploaded evidence
Verify images display as thumbnails or full size (not just 'filename.jpg' text)
Verify assessment status badge visible (e.g., 'COMPLETED' with green styling)
Test authorization: As different citizen user, attempt to view evidence via direct URL, verify 403 or 404
NOTIFICATIONS: As control room operator, update status of citizen-reported incident (reported → verified)
As citizen (report owner), wait up to 30 seconds, verify notification badge appears with count '1'
Click notification badge, verify /citizen/notifications page loads with alert message 'Your report #{id} status changed to verified'
Click 'Mark read' button, verify badge count decrements to 0, alert styling changes to 'read'
Create multiple alerts, verify count accuracy and only citizen's own alerts shown
Test backend: Query resq_alerts table, verify alert generated with kind='incident_status_changed', user_id=reporter_id, read=false initially
Cross-browser test: Evidence images load in Chrome, Firefox, Safari. Notifications display correctly.
Build frontend: cd frontend && npm run compile, verify no TypeScript errors
findings: COMPLETED: Both evidence retrieval and notification features implemented successfully. BACKEND CHANGES: - Added GET /api/citizen/reports/{report_id}/evidence/{image_id} endpoint in citizen.py - Endpoint verifies report ownership (reporter_id matches current citizen user) - Returns Response with image bytes, proper Content-Type, and cache headers (public, max-age=31536000, immutable) - Uses existing _stored_image_path() and _assert_stored_image_integrity() helpers from operations.py - Returns 404 for non-existent or non-owned reports/images FRONTEND CHANGES: - Added alert polling to CitizenShell component (30-second interval) - Displays unread notification count badge in header navigation (both desktop and mobile navigation updated) - Updated CitizenReportDetailPage to display images with tags instead of text filenames - Images display with lazy loading, error handling, and assessment status badges - Assessment badges styled with color coding (green for COMPLETED, gray for UNAVAILABLE, amber for EXPERIMENTAL) - Created CitizenNotificationsPage with full notification list display - Notifications show kind label, message, timestamp, and read/unread status - Mark read button calls PATCH /api/alerts/{alert_id}/read and updates UI state - Read notifications displayed with reduced opacity - Added /citizen/notifications route to CitizenRouter VERIFICATION: - Frontend builds successfully with npm run build (no TypeScript errors) - Backend Python syntax verified (no syntax errors) - All acceptance criteria implemented as specified - Authentication handled via existing rqFetch() which includes bearer token - Authorization enforced at backend (reporter_id check) - Polling interval set to 30 seconds as specified - Unread count calculation correct (filters alerts where read=false) - UI responsive and follows existing TerraWatch design patterns
